sense: towards a place or a person: go to, come to

terms.gloss: to, up to (a place or a person)
evidence: Ter. Ad. 970: ehō, accēde hūc ad mē
Cic. Fam. 9.4.1: tū sī minus ad nōs, nōs accurrēmus ad tē
terms.comment: Ad takes you to a place or a person, up to it or into its presence; in with the accusative takes you into it (see into). Ad forum īre, go to the forum; ad mē venī, come to me, and so to my house (see at the house of). Giving or saying something to someone is the dative, with no preposition: dā mihi.

terms.gloss: home, to the country; to Rome
terms.comment: Names of towns and small islands, domus and rūs take no preposition: Rōmam proficīscī, domum redīre. Ad with a town’s name is to its neighbourhood, up to it: ad Capuam.

evidence: Vulg. Gen. 28.15: redūcam tē in terram hanc
terms.comment: Of a country or a region Latin goes “into” it: in Graeciam proficīscī, go to Greece.

phrases.latin: ego eō ad forum, nisi quid vīs
phrases.english: I’m off to the forum, unless you want something

phrases.latin: tū sī minus ad nōs, nōs accurrēmus ad tē
phrases.english: if you don’t come to us, we will hurry to you

phrases.latin: Abī domum, ac deōs comprecāre ut uxōrem arcessās: abī.
phrases.english: Go home and pray to the gods, so that you can fetch your bride: go!

phrases.latin: īte domum saturae, venit Hesperus, īte capellae
phrases.english: go home, my well-fed goats, the evening star is coming, go

phrases.latin: Et erō custōs tuus quōcumque perrēxeris, et redūcam tē in terram hanc
phrases.english: And I will keep you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land
